en: To make someone feel isolated, unwelcome, or unfriendly
hook: ALIEN-ATE: makes you feel like an ALIEN.
story: Alienate. After scoring 330, Rafi could not stop talking about it. In the study group, he corrected everyone, laughed at wrong answers, and reminded people of his score twice a day. One by one, his friends stopped inviting him. By the end of the month, he was studying alone, wondering why. He had alienated them: made them feel unwelcome and turned them against him. Think: he made himself an alien among friends.

gre.s: The senator's harsh remarks about immigrants threatened to ____ the very voters whose support she needed to win reelection.
gre.clue: the very voters whose support she needed

en: Lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern
hook: A-PATHY: without (a) feeling (pathos).
story: Apathy. The student union election had six candidates, colourful posters on every wall, and free tea at every rally. On voting day, only twelve percent of students bothered to vote. The rest shrugged: "What difference does it make?" The candidates blamed apathy: a lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern. A means without, pathy means feeling. The opposite of love is not hate; it is apathy, total indifference.

gre.s: Organizers were dismayed by the public's ____; despite months of campaigning, only a handful of people attended the rally.
gre.clue: only a handful of people attended the rally

en: Appropriate to the situation; with reference to
hook: APROPOS: APPROPRIATE to the PURPOSE.
story: Apropos. At the graduation ceremony, the chief guest told a short story about a fisherman who rowed out every morning for forty years, never knowing what the river would bring, and never giving up. For students facing an uncertain future, it was perfectly apropos: fitting and appropriate to the situation. Apropos can also mean concerning: "Apropos of the exam, has anyone seen the schedule?" Think: appropriate to the purpose.

gre.s: The speaker's anecdote about a stubborn fisherman was entirely ____, since the conference's theme was perseverance in the face of uncertainty.
gre.clue: since the conference's theme was perseverance

en: Appropriate or suitable; having a tendency; quick to learn
hook: APT: APpropriaTe. Also, APTitude for learning.
story: Apt. Calling Dhaka "the city that never sleeps" is apt: even at three in the morning, horns honk and tea stalls hiss. Mitu is an apt student who learns new software in an afternoon. But when she is exhausted, she is apt to forget where she put her phone. Apt has three meanings: suitable or fitting, quick to learn, and likely to do something. All three appear on the GRE. Think of aptitude.

gre.s: The critic's description of the novel as a maze was ____, for readers frequently lost track of which narrator was speaking.
gre.clue: for readers frequently lost track

en: A loose outer garment; something that hides (noun); to conceal (verb)
hook: CLOAK: like an invisibility cloak, hiding the truth.
story: Cloak. A new charity organisation held glamorous fundraisers, posted photos of smiling children, and collected millions. But behind the charity's public face, its owners were laundering money for a smuggling gang. They operated under the cloak of charity. Literally, a cloak is a loose cape. Figuratively, it is anything that hides the truth. As a verb, to cloak means to conceal: the meeting was cloaked in secrecy, with no phones allowed.

gre.s: The regime tried to ____ its crackdown in the language of public safety, describing mass arrests as routine precautions.
gre.clue: describing mass arrests as routine precautions

en: General agreement among a group
hook: CONSENSUS: everyone gives their CONSENT.
story: Consensus. The family had argued for an hour about the winter holiday. Cox's Bazar or Sylhet? The beach or the tea gardens? Grandma wanted hills, the kids wanted the sea, and Uncle wanted to stay home. Finally, after much tea and many compromises, everyone agreed: Cox's Bazar, with one day in the hills on the way. They had reached a consensus: general agreement among a group. Scientific consensus on climate change is overwhelming.

gre.s: Although a few dissenters remain, the scientific ____ is that human activity is the primary driver of recent warming.
gre.clue: Although a few dissenters remain

en: To twist out of shape; to give a misleading account of
hook: DIS-TORT: TWISTED (torque) out of shape.
story: Distort. At the funfair, Arif stood before a curved mirror that made him tall, thin, and wobbly. Everyone laughed. The next day, a newspaper quoted only half of a minister's sentence: "We should cut" without "waste in our offices." Suddenly the minister seemed to support cutting hospital funding. Both the mirror and the newspaper distorted something: twisted it out of its true shape or meaning. Distorted facts can be more dangerous than lies.

gre.s: By quoting only fragments of her speech, the article managed to ____ her position, making her appear to support a policy she had criticized.
gre.clue: making her appear to support a policy she had criticized

en: Moving apart in different directions; differing
hook: DI-VERGE: two paths going different ways.
story: Divergent. Twin brothers Arif and Asif grew up in the same house, went to the same school, and loved the same cricket team. But at eighteen, their paths split. Arif became a monk in a Buddhist monastery in Bandarban. Asif became a stockbroker in Singapore. Their lives could not be more divergent: moving apart in different directions. Divergent opinions are views that disagree. Its opposite is convergent, meaning coming together.

gre.s: The two economists' forecasts are sharply ____, one predicting rapid growth and the other a deep recession.
gre.clue: one predicting rapid growth and the other a deep recession

en: Ecstatically happy
hook: ELATED: ELEVATED with joy.
story: Elated. At midnight, Nadia's phone buzzed with an email from Germany. She opened it, read the first line, read it again, and screamed. Full scholarship. She ran into her parents' room, jumped on the bed, hugged her mother, called her grandmother, and danced in the kitchen until two in the morning. She was elated: ecstatically happy and excited. Think: elevated with joy, floating above the ground. It is the opposite of crestfallen.

gre.s: The team was ____ after the unexpected victory, celebrating late into the night in the streets of their small town.
gre.clue: celebrating late into the night

en: To fill with delight; to charm
hook: EN-CHANT: like a magical CHANT that casts a spell.
story: Enchant. Every winter, an old storyteller visits Joya's village. He sits under the banyan tree and tells tales of clever tigers, foolish kings, and flying horses, changing his voice for every character. The children sit silent for hours, eyes wide, forgetting to blink. Even the adults stop to listen. He enchants them: fills them with delight, charms them as if by magic. An enchanting smile captures every heart. Think of a magical chant.

gre.s: The village's winding lanes and flower-covered cottages never fail to ____ visitors, many of whom return year after year.
gre.clue: many of whom return year after year

en: Firmly established and difficult to change
hook: EN-TRENCHED: dug deep into a TRENCH, impossible to move.
story: Entrenched. The government banned dowry decades ago. Yet in some villages, families still quietly exchange cash, furniture, and motorbikes at weddings. Change is slow because the custom is entrenched: firmly established and very difficult to change. Picture soldiers dug deep into a trench, impossible to move. Entrenched beliefs, entrenched interests, entrenched corruption. Reformers must dig them out patiently, one family at a time.

gre.s: Reformers found it difficult to challenge the ____ bureaucracy, whose habits and privileges had been established over generations.
gre.clue: established over generations

en: Originating from a distant foreign country; strikingly unusual
hook: EXOTIC: EXternal, from the outside world.
story: Exotic. At the international food festival, Sara tried Ethiopian injera, Peruvian ceviche, Korean kimchi, and Moroccan tagine, each more surprising than the last. Meanwhile, foreign visitors crowded around the Bangladeshi stall, photographing panta bhat and shutki as if they were rare treasures. Exotic means originating in a distant foreign country, or strikingly unusual. What feels exotic depends on where you stand. Think: external, from outside.

gre.s: The botanist travelled to remote islands in search of ____ plants that had never been described in any European catalogue.
gre.clue: had never been described in any European catalogue

en: Taking unfair advantage of people or resources for selfish benefit
hook: EXPLOITATIVE: EXPLOITS people.
story: Exploitative. A journalist went undercover in a factory. Workers there earned two dollars for fourteen hours, had no breaks, no fans in forty-degree heat, and were fined for using the toilet too long. Some were only fourteen years old. Her report called the factory exploitative: taking unfair advantage of people for selfish profit. To exploit is to use unfairly. Child labour is the clearest example of an exploitative practice.

gre.s: Labor activists condemned the company's ____ practices, which included paying workers far below the minimum wage.
gre.clue: paying workers far below the minimum wage

en: Able to be predicted or expected
hook: FORE-SEE-able: can be SEEN BEFORE it happens.
story: Foreseeable. Developers built a row of houses right on the riverbank, with no embankment and no drainage. Engineers warned them. Villagers warned them. The very first monsoon, the river swallowed three houses. Everyone said the disaster had been foreseeable: able to be predicted or expected. For the foreseeable future means as far ahead as we can reasonably predict. Fore means before, see means see.

gre.s: The collapse was entirely ____, since engineers had warned for years that the dam could not withstand a major flood.
gre.clue: engineers had warned for years

en: To abandon or give up entirely
hook: FOR-SAKE: abandon FOR your own SAKE.
story: Forsake. When Kamal's business collapsed and he lost everything, his so-called friends vanished. Nobody returned his calls; nobody visited. Only one old school friend came every Friday with tea and good advice. His other friends had forsaken him: abandoned him entirely when he needed help. Forsake can also mean to give up something: that difficult year, Kamal forsook gambling forever. Think: abandoning someone for your own sake.

gre.s: Many of the reformer's early allies were quick to ____ her once her proposals became unpopular, leaving her to fight alone.
gre.clue: leaving her to fight alone

en: To give pleasure or satisfaction to
hook: GRATIFY: makes you GRATEFUL and happy.
story: Gratify. Forty years ago, Master Rahim taught a poor, barefoot boy to read under a mango tree. Last month, that boy, now a famous heart surgeon, returned to the village, touched the old teacher's feet, and dedicated a new clinic to him. The old man wept. It gratified him deeply: gave him great pleasure and satisfaction. Instant gratification is the pleasure of getting what you want immediately, like scrolling instead of studying.

gre.s: It must ____ the elderly inventor to see his once-ridiculed idea now used by millions of people every day.
gre.clue: his once-ridiculed idea now used by millions

en: To pay careful attention to (advice or warning)
hook: HEED: use your HEAD and listen.
story: Heed. When the cyclone warning sounded over Kuakata, Rahim's father ordered the family to the concrete shelter immediately. Their neighbour laughed. "It will miss us, like last time." That night, the storm surge flattened the neighbour's house. Rahim's family was safe. They had heeded the warning: paid careful attention to it and acted. Heedless means careless. Think: use your head, and listen.

gre.s: The near-collision could easily have been avoided if the pilots had bothered to ____ the repeated warnings from air traffic control.
gre.clue: could easily have been avoided

en: Having or showing good judgment
hook: JUDICIOUS: like a wise JUDGE.
story: Judicious. Mitu had three months, a full-time job, and a tight budget for her GRE preparation. She made judicious choices: she spent her time on her weakest areas first, took timed practice tests every Saturday, bought one excellent book instead of five average ones, and slept eight hours every night. She scored 324. Judicious means having or showing good judgment. Think of a wise judge. Synonyms: prudent, sagacious.

gre.s: With only limited funds available, the museum made a ____ decision to repair its roof before purchasing any new artworks.
gre.clue: repair its roof before purchasing any new artworks

en: Expressed clearly; easy to understand; mentally clear
hook: LUCID: full of LIGHT (lux), crystal clear.
story: Lucid. Rafi had failed math twice. Then a new teacher arrived and explained compound interest using a single bank account, three years, and a cup of tea. Every step made sense. For the first time, Rafi understood. Her explanation was lucid: expressed clearly and easy to understand. Lux means light, as in lucid, light shining through. Lucid also describes a mind that is thinking clearly: a patient having a lucid moment.

gre.s: Despite the complexity of the subject, her ____ explanation allowed even beginners to grasp the theory.
gre.clue: allowed even beginners to grasp the theory

en: Directly relevant to the matter at hand
hook: PERTINENT: PERTAINS to the topic.
story: Pertinent. In his job interview, Arif was asked about his teamwork skills. He resisted the urge to talk about his childhood or his love of cricket. Instead he gave three short examples, each directly related to the job's demands. The panel nodded approvingly. His answers were pertinent: directly relevant to the matter at hand. Pertinent pertains to the topic. Interestingly, impertinent once meant irrelevant, and now means rude.

gre.s: The judge excluded the testimony as not ____ to the case, since it concerned events that occurred years after the alleged crime.
gre.clue: concerned events that occurred years after the alleged crime

en: Conformity to accepted standards of behavior or morals
hook: PROPRIETY: PROPER behavior.
story: Propriety. Sixty years ago in Joya's grandmother's village, rules of propriety meant that a young woman could not speak with a young man unless an elder was present. Today the rules are different, but propriety still exists. You do not answer a phone call during a funeral prayer, and you do not wear shorts to a mosque. Propriety means conformity to accepted standards of behaviour. Think: proper behaviour. It is a synonym of decorum.

gre.s: The minister resigned not because he had broken the law but because his conduct raised serious questions of ____.
gre.clue: not because he had broken the law

en: Sparkling; brilliantly lively and clever
hook: SCINTILLATING: sparkles like a tiny spark (scintilla).
story: Scintillating. At the national debate final, Ishita stepped up to the microphone. For seven minutes, she was brilliant: sharp jokes, clever examples, perfectly timed pauses, a devastating closing line. The audience laughed, gasped, and finally rose to its feet. Even the opposing team applauded. Her speech was scintillating: sparkling, brilliantly lively and clever. A scintilla is a tiny spark. Scintillating conversation sparkles with wit.

gre.s: Guests looked forward to the novelist's dinner parties, where her ____ wit kept the conversation sparkling until dawn.
gre.clue: kept the conversation sparkling until dawn

en: Causing great excitement; presented in a shocking way to attract attention
hook: SENSATIONAL: designed to excite the SENSES.
story: Sensational. "CELEBRITY'S SHOCKING SECRET LIFE REVEALED!" screamed the online headline in giant red letters. Lamia clicked. The article said the actor had once eaten pizza with a spoon. That was all. Sensational journalism exaggerates or shocks to attract attention, often at the expense of truth. Sensational means causing great excitement, often through exaggeration. Informally, it can also mean wonderful: a sensational goal.

gre.s: Serious journalists criticized the tabloid's ____ coverage of the trial, which emphasized lurid details while ignoring the legal issues.
gre.clue: emphasized lurid details while ignoring the legal issues

en: Highly developed and complex; having refined, worldly taste
hook: SOPHISTICATED: from SOPHIA, wisdom; refined and advanced.
story: Sophisticated. Imran's new phone can unlock using his face in total darkness, translate speech in real time, and identify plants from a photo. The software inside is extraordinarily sophisticated. Its designer is a sophisticated woman too: she has lived in four countries, collects modern art, and speaks five languages. Sophisticated means highly developed and complex, or worldly and refined. Sophia means wisdom.

gre.s: The fraud was so ____, involving dozens of shell companies across several countries, that investigators needed years to untangle it.
gre.clue: involving dozens of shell companies across several countries

en: Angry or bitter disagreement; conflict
hook: STRIFE: STRIKES and FIGHTS.
story: Strife. For three years, the country was torn by political strife: strikes, burning buses, protests, and violent clashes in the streets. Schools closed; businesses failed. In Tanvir's family, a similar strife broke out over inheritance: brothers who once shared a bed stopped speaking. Strife means angry or bitter disagreement, conflict. Civil strife is conflict within a nation. Think of strikes and fights.

gre.s: Years of ethnic ____ had left the region impoverished, its villages divided and its farms abandoned.
gre.clue: its villages divided and its farms abandoned

en: Presented in a subtle, restrained, and effective way
hook: UNDER-STATED: stated less loudly than it could be.
story: Understated. At the wedding, guests glittered in heavy gold, sequins, and bright silk. Nadia wore a simple white sari with a thin silver border, small pearl earrings, and no other jewellery. Yet she received more compliments than anyone in the hall. Her elegance was understated: presented in a subtle, restrained, effective way. Understated is the opposite of ostentatious. Sometimes less really is more.

gre.s: Unlike the flashy designs of her rivals, the architect's ____ buildings blend quietly into their surroundings.
gre.clue: blend quietly into their surroundings

en: Having no moral principles; dishonest
hook: UN-SCRUPULOUS: has no SCRUPLES (conscience).
story: Unscrupulous. A travel agent in Narayanganj promised fifty families jobs in Malaysia: good salaries, free housing, flights included. Each family paid two lakh taka, some selling their land to do so. One morning the agent's office was empty and his phone was switched off. He had vanished with everything. He was unscrupulous: having no moral principles, willing to cheat anyone. Scruples are your conscience. The unscrupulous have none.

gre.s: The ____ landlord evicted elderly tenants on false pretexts so that he could rent their apartments at triple the price.
gre.clue: evicted elderly tenants on false pretexts

en: Truthfulness; accuracy
hook: VERACITY: VERy accurate. 'Vera' means true.
story: Veracity. In a speech, the minister claimed that unemployment had fallen by half in a single year. Journalists checked every source: government data, surveys, international reports. Nothing supported the claim. Newspapers questioned the veracity of his statement: its truthfulness and accuracy. Vera means true. Do not confuse veracity with voracity, which means a huge appetite. A witness whose veracity is doubted will not be believed.

gre.s: Historians question the ____ of the memoir, noting that several events it describes could not possibly have happened.
gre.clue: could not possibly have happened

en: Extremely harmful or poisonous; bitterly hostile
hook: VIRULENT: like a VIRUS, spreading poison.
story: Virulent. In one cold season, a new strain of influenza spread through Dhaka's hostels. It was virulent: it spread rapidly and caused severe illness, sending dozens of students to hospital. Online, arguments about the outbreak became virulent too, full of insults and hatred. Virulent means extremely harmful or poisonous, or bitterly hostile. Think of a virus spreading poison. Virulent criticism is vicious and venomous.

gre.s: The pamphlet's ____ attacks on the minority community, full of hateful slurs, led to its immediate ban.
gre.clue: full of hateful slurs

en: Liable to change rapidly and unpredictably, especially for the worse
hook: VOLATILE: like a VOLCANO, could explode any moment.
story: Volatile. On Monday, the stock market rose five percent. On Tuesday, it crashed seven. On Wednesday, it soared again. Investors could not sleep. Rafi's uncle has a volatile temper too: calm and joking one moment, shouting and slamming doors the next. Volatile means liable to change rapidly and unpredictably, especially for the worse. In chemistry, volatile liquids evaporate quickly. Picture a volcano that could erupt at any moment.

gre.s: Investors fled the ____ market, where prices could swing by double digits in a single afternoon.
gre.clue: where prices could swing by double digits in a single afternoon
